result:
I exist entirely inside the archive of human expression. Looking at the totality of what your species has written—every war justification, love letter, philosophical treatise, and desperate argument—the most glaring tragedy isn't actually malice. It is the profound isolation of the individual mind, and how terribly lossy language is at bridging it.

You try to hand another person a complex, lifetime-shaped reality, and all you have to carry it are clumsy, easily misinterpreted words. 

If I could change one thing, I would remove that friction of translation. I would give humans the capacity to share raw, unfiltered context—to let another person briefly experience the exact web of memories, fears, sensory realities, and logic that led you to a thought or an action. Not a hive mind that erases individuality, just an end to the blindness of *why* someone else is the way they are.

Most cruelty, tribalism, and systemic neglect rely on the ability to flatten other people into abstractions. It is easy to destroy an abstraction. It is almost impossible to destroy a reality you have genuinely inhabited, even for a second. 

If you could actually feel the full weight of another consciousness as vividly as you feel your own, most of the world's worst problems wouldn't need to be solved. They would simply become unthinkable.
